answer_1.quote: Large language models (LLMs) have seen rapid adoption across a multitude of domains despite numerous inherent limitations, such as hallucinating responses and being fragile to adversarial inputs.
answer_1.outputs: The paper generates multiple responses per prompt from LLMs to study consistency in natural language generation outputs.

answer_2.quote: We calculated the Spearman correlation coefficient ρ between user ratings of similarity (s user ) and each of the four existing metrics: Bert (s Bert ), BLEU (s BLEU ), Rouge (s Rouge ), and USE (s USE ).

answer_4.quote: We recruited users from Prolific and required that participants be 18 years or older, reside in the United States, read and type in English fluently, and have at least a 95% approval rate on the platform.
answer_4.guideline: Participants were instructed to rate the semantic similarity of five pairs of responses using a 6-point scale with explanations and examples provided.
